introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - Ordinary Level Examination. Computer Science (0595), Paper 3 (practical), June 2023. Duration: two and a half hours. Do all the tasks (Task I, Task II and Task III) specified in the question paper.**

Enter the information required in the shaded boxes. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. All written answers should be provided in the spaces provided in this question booklet. Calculators are NOT allowed.

The booklet reproduced here contains four versions of the same practical paper, headed Group One, Group Two, Group Three and Group Four (booklets 23/0595/3/Grp 1 to Grp 4); a candidate sits only ONE group. Each version has three tasks: Task I (word processing), Task II (spreadsheet) and Task III (a short exercise on HTML, on a database or on a C or Pascal program). The working files named in the tasks (the picture UN.jpg, the pictures of the authors) are supplied on the day; they are not reproduced in the printed paper.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**GROUP FOUR - TASK I (20 marks)**

Figure 1 is an article on the history of Algebra. Your task is to type, edit and format the text as requested.

> **What is Algebra?**
>
> Algebra is a branch of mathematics in which you use symbols, usually letters of the alphabet, to solve mathematical problems. These letters, or symbols, are placed in the problem to show an unknown.
>
> The roots of the word, algebra, can be found in Medieval Latin and the Arabic word, 'Al Jabr', which means 'the reduction'. The word was first used as early as 1551.
>
> The history of algebra can be divided into three parts:
>
> - The rhetorical, or written stage, where only words were used in equations
> - The syncopated, or shortened, stage, where some symbols were used in equations
> - The symbolic or modern stage
>
> The beginnings of algebra have been traced back as far as ancient Egypt and Babylon. No one person has been given complete credit for the subject of algebra; however, two of the best-known 'Fathers of Algebra' are Abu Jaafar Mohammad Ibn Mousa Al Khwarizmi and Diophantus, who made contributions to the second stage of algebra. Al Khwarizmi developed methods for balancing and reducing algebraic equations and introduced algorithms, which are mathematical operations or rules. Diophantus wrote 13 books entitled 'Arithmetica', which contain problems and solutions that have furthered algebraic notation.
>
> *Source: https://study.com/academy/lesson/history-of-algebra-lesson-for-kids.html*

*Figure 1 (the text of the article, printed inside a bordered box).*

questions.enonce_markdown: Name the word processor, including the version, installed on your computer. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The answer depends on the computer used in the examination hall: write the real name and version of the word processor that is installed, as shown in *File* > *Account* or *Help* > *About* (for example "Microsoft Word" followed by its version number, or "LibreOffice Writer" followed by its version number).

Marking idea (1 mark): the name of a word processor with a version number.

questions.enonce_markdown: Launch the word processor software and type without borders, the text of Figure 1. Use a line spacing of 1.5. *[7 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Open the word processor and a new blank document.

1. Type the heading **What is Algebra?**, the three paragraphs, the sentence "The history of algebra can be divided into three parts:", the three list lines, the last long paragraph and the source line, exactly as printed. Do **not** type or draw the box that surrounds the text in Figure 1: "without borders" means that the typed text has no frame around it.
2. Select all (*Ctrl + A*) and set the line spacing to **1.5** (*Paragraph* > *Line spacing* > 1.5 lines).
3. Check the spelling (names such as Al Khwarizmi, Diophantus, Arithmetica are correct as typed).

Marking idea (7 marks): heading and three paragraphs (2); the three list lines (1); last paragraph (2); source line (1); line spacing 1.5 and no border (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Describe briefly how to add page borders to a word document. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
In *Microsoft Word*: open the **Design** tab (or *Page Layout*) > click **Page Borders** > in the *Borders and Shading* window, *Page Border* tab, choose a setting (for example **Box**), a style, a colour and a width > *Apply to: Whole document* > **OK**. In *LibreOffice Writer*: *Format* > *Page Style* > *Borders* tab > choose the line arrangement and style > *OK*.

Marking idea (2 marks): the Page Borders command is found (1); a border style is chosen and applied to the document (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Format the title of the typed text as follows: font type Arial or any sans serif font, font size 20, centre-aligned, bold and underlined. *[4 marks]*
Format the last paragraph to have 2 columns. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The last paragraph is the one that begins "The beginnings of algebra..." and ends with "...algebraic notation." (the source line is not part of it).

1. Select this paragraph only.
2. *Layout* tab > **Columns** > **Two**. (In *LibreOffice Writer*: *Format* > *Columns* > 2.) The word processor puts the selected text between two section breaks and divides it into two columns of text.
3. Check that the title and the other paragraphs are still on one column.

Marking idea (3 marks): the right paragraph selected (1); two columns applied (1); the rest of the text unchanged (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Insert the following text in brackets, just after the text "Medieval Latin": "form of Latin used in Roman Catholic Western Europe during the Middle Ages". *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Click right after "Medieval Latin" in the second paragraph and type (with the opening bracket, a space and the closing bracket):

`Medieval Latin (form of Latin used in Roman Catholic Western Europe during the Middle Ages) and the Arabic word...`

In the printed instruction the inserted text is in italics, which can be reproduced (*Ctrl + I*).

Marking idea (1 mark): the text inserted in brackets at the right place.

questions.enonce_markdown: Insert the source of the passage (the last line) as a footer on the page. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. Select the last line **Source: https://study.com/academy/lesson/history-of-algebra-lesson-for-kids.html** and cut it (*Ctrl + X*).
2. *Insert* > **Footer** > *Blank* (or *Edit Footer*), paste the line (*Ctrl + V*) in the footer area and close the footer.

The source now appears at the bottom of the page, outside the body of the text.

Marking idea (2 marks): a footer created (1); it contains the source line, which is no longer in the body (1).
